en.note: Distinguish an apology from sympathy using nearby cues.
Keep the draft for sympathy. For an apology or request for clarification, review the alternatives.

en.draft: Det gør mig ondt for din far.
suggestions: Det gør mig ondt at høre om din far.
en.note: Use if the scene expresses sympathy.

en.source: I'm sorry about last night. I shouldn't have done that.
en.draft: Undskyld om aftenen i går. Jeg burde ikke have gjort det.
suggestions: Undskyld for i går aftes. Jeg burde ikke have gjort det.
en.note: Apology for the speaker’s own actions; check timing and register.
Check whether the speaker is confirming an instruction, agreeing or talking about possession.

en.source: So don't make a liar out of me, Colonel.
en.draft: Så lav ikke en løgn af mig, oberst.
suggestions: Så lad mig ikke stå som en løgner, oberst.
en.note: The speaker wants to be able to keep a promise.

en.source: Maybe you take it down a notch.
en.draft: Måske skal du sætte det lidt ned.
suggestions: Måske skulle du lige skrue lidt ned.
en.note: Check whether the speaker means to tone down their behavior or turn down a setting.

en.source: I'm good. You know me. Work, work, work.
en.draft: Jeg er god. Du kender mig. Arbejde, arbejde, arbejde.
suggestions: Jeg har det fint. Du kender mig. Arbejde, arbejde, arbejde.
en.note: Use when the speaker is saying how they are.

en.source: I'm sick of your rules! Give me a break!
en.draft: Jeg er mæt af dine regler! Giv mig en pause!
suggestions: Jeg er træt af dine regler! Hold nu op!
en.note: Use if the speaker is exasperated.
Use if the speaker is acknowledging information. Keep the existing meaning if they literally see something.

suggestions: Det var lige ved at gå galt.
en.note: Use for a narrow escape. The draft can work for a close contest.

en.draft: Jeg kan ikke regne på det.
en.replacement: Det ville jeg ikke regne med.

en.note: Use if the speaker emphatically agrees. Keep the literal meaning when asking someone to repeat something.
Use if the speaker is warning against going too far. Keep the draft if a physical object is involved.
Use if the speaker is warning against going too far. Check context for a physical action.
